content.value_statement: Logseq Markdown graphs can be hard to move into the Database format without losing structure. This skill helps users plan, import, validate, and troubleshoot migrations with clear steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains when and why to migrate a Logseq Markdown graph to Database format.
Lists pre-migration checks for pages, properties, tags, templates, and queries.
Compares migration strategies for small, large, and messy graphs.
Guides import choices for tags, namespaces, and property typing.
Provides validation ideas for page counts, orphaned blocks, and migrated properties.
Troubleshoots common issues such as broken references and changed query attributes.
limitations: It does not run the Logseq migration or modify graph files automatically.
It depends on Logseq Database behavior that may change during alpha releases.
It cannot guarantee complete data recovery without verified backups.
Plugin compatibility advice may require checking each installed plugin.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Personal Graph Migration
use_cases.description: Review graph structure, create backups, and choose import settings before moving a personal knowledge base to Database format.

use_cases.title: Validate a Team Knowledge Base
use_cases.description: Compare important pages, properties, tags, and queries after migration so team workflows keep working.

use_cases.title: Plan Complex Graph Cleanup
use_cases.description: Decide how to handle namespaces, classes, typed properties, and old queries in a large or inconsistent Logseq graph.

prompt_templates.title: Check Migration Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me decide whether my Logseq Markdown graph is ready for Database migration. Ask for the graph details you need, then give me a checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Import Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: I am importing a Logseq Markdown graph into Database format. Help me choose settings for tags, namespaces, properties, and references.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Migration Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: My Logseq Database migration finished, but some references, properties, or queries look wrong. Help me diagnose the likely causes and fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Staged Migration Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged migration plan for a large Logseq graph with many namespaces, templates, queries, and plugins. Include validation checkpoints and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: I have a small Logseq graph and want to move from Markdown to Database format.
output_examples.output: The response outlines backup steps, export preparation, import choices, and a short validation checklist for page counts, tags, and properties.

output_examples.input: My migrated graph has broken page links and changed query results.
output_examples.output: The response identifies likely namespace or attribute changes, suggests checks for renamed pages, and explains how to update old query assumptions.

output_examples.input: I manage a large graph with plugins and shared workflows.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a parallel migration strategy, plugin compatibility review, critical page validation, and a rollback plan using the Markdown graph backup.

best_practices: Create and verify a full graph backup before every migration test.
Test with a small subset before migrating an active or large graph.
Validate pages, blocks, tags, properties, queries, and critical workflows after import.
anti_patterns: Migrating the only copy of a graph without a verified backup.
Assuming all Markdown tags should become Database classes.
Deleting the original Markdown graph before completing post-migration checks.

faq.question: Does this skill migrate my Logseq graph automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning, decision support, validation steps, and troubleshooting guidance. You still perform the migration in Logseq.

faq.question: Can it help choose between tag references and classes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains the tradeoffs and helps decide which tags should become classes based on your graph structure.

faq.question: Does it cover namespace changes during migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes flattening and hierarchy choices, plus common issues when similar names collide.

faq.question: Can it validate migrated data?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests checks for page counts, orphaned blocks, migrated properties, references, and query behavior.

faq.question: Is the guidance current for Logseq Database alpha?
faq.answer: The skill describes Logseq Database as alpha and recommends checking current documentation before relying on migration behavior.

faq.question: Will it guarantee plugin compatibility?
faq.answer: No. It flags plugin compatibility as variable and recommends testing important plugins before moving production workflows.
